reader_notes: Long and dense for an ELF passage (~900 words of literary-journalistic British English), but every sentence survives a second read and the argument (volume vs. timing/spread) is carried cleanly from the opening to the closing line.

Q4 is the hardest step: it needs two sentences combined (unequal travel times to Millstake, plus 'a chain of ponds on one tributary fills, spills and empties on a single schedule'). The inference is fair and single-valued, but it is the one question where a hurried reader could land on D.
